title: Evidence detail endpoint rejects requests for an evidence ID belonging to another organization
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) each with at least one evidence item
Valid JWT for a user in org A
steps: As an org A user, call GET /api/evidence/:id using an evidence ID that belongs to org B
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403/404 — no evidence metadata or file content from org B is returned in the response body.

title: Upload endpoint rejects executable file types disguised with an allowed extension
steps: Attempt to upload a file with .pdf extension whose content is actually a Windows PE executable
expectedResult: Upload is rejected based on magic-byte/content-type sniffing, not filename extension alone.

title: Presigned-upload confirm rejects an s3Key outside the caller's organization prefix
description: confirmPresignedUpload (evidence-upload.controller.js) checks s3Key.startsWith('evidence/{req.orgId}/') before accepting the file record. Regression guard for this IDOR protection on the direct-to-S3 presigned flow.
preconditions: Valid JWT for a user in org A
A presigned upload URL generated for org A's own s3Key prefix
steps: As an org A user, call POST /evidence/upload/:evidenceId/files/confirm with a forged s3Key beginning with 'evidence/{orgB-id}/' instead of org A's prefix
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 's3Key does not belong to this organization' — no file record is pushed onto any evidence document.

title: Presigned-upload confirm does not verify declared MIME type against the actual S3 object content
description: Unlike the multer upload path (validateMagicBytes reads the first 4100 bytes of every buffered file), confirmPresignedUpload only calls S3.getFileMetadata(s3Key) for size/etag/checksum and stores the client-supplied mimeType verbatim — it never compares that to the object's actual ContentType or performs a magic-byte check. A file uploaded directly to S3 with a spoofed Content-Type can be confirmed and stored as if it were a benign type.
preconditions: A presigned upload URL for a PDF has been generated
An HTML/JS payload has been PUT directly to that S3 key with Content-Type: application/pdf declared at the S3 PUT step
steps: Upload the HTML/JS payload directly to the presigned S3 URL, declaring Content-Type: application/pdf
Call POST /evidence/upload/:evidenceId/files/confirm with mimeType='application/pdf' and the matching s3Key
expectedResult: Current behavior: the confirm call succeeds and the file is recorded as mimeType 'application/pdf' with no server-side verification against the object's real content — this is a gap versus the multer path's magic-byte enforcement and should be flagged for remediation (add a headObject + file-type check before accepting the confirm).
